analysis:
The only change in docs/developer/test.md is a documentation edit around head lines 142-153 (CI cache-save policy and MiMo audio gate triggers), which sits outside the two supplied text units (lines 932-1846). The supplied units are unchanged surrounding test documentation. I read them in full and found no security-relevant behavior change.

CI cache policy change per the patch: only pushes to dev or master save a build cache, and pull requests restore but never save. This narrows cache-poisoning exposure from PR-authored cache entries, so it is a mild improvement and not a regression. It does not touch provider runtime threats such as T-041 (SSD prefix cache), which concerns the provider's encrypted KV cache and not the CI build cache.

The MiMo audio gate now runs only when its inputs change or on master pushes. This is test coverage scope, not a runtime control. The documented skip for out-of-scope PRs could in theory reduce coverage, but the path list (MIMO_AUDIO in scripts/ci-component-paths.py) is not in the supplied evidence. I cannot verify it, so I record it as an unverified contract and not a finding.

The documentation in the supplied units describes TB-012 add-on hold socket tests (lines 932-956) and notes that the peer check is exercised only negatively. The docs state this limitation explicitly, and no code changed. It is consistent with T-059/T-060 and I found no invalidated assumption. No new attack surface, secrets, or threat-model gaps were identified in the supplied lines. Remaining open question: whether the CI classifier path list adequately covers audio/media inputs. That is outside this documentation diff.
